Definition: i.e. G2443 and G3361; in order (or so) that not:--albeit not, lest, that, no(-t, (-thing)).
BiblicalUsage: Hína mḗ is two words standing together — ἵνα, “that”, and μή, “not” — making “so that not”, or “lest”. The pair stands together 85 times in the Greek New Testament; John and 1 John show it in use.
TheologicalSignificance: I read hína mḗ plainly: so that not, lest — and I leave it there.
